about: An event's payload carries an enum field beside a list of records its schema's second revision added: the enum field is a value of its enum there as in a schema of one entry per field. A guard compares it with `===` to a variant, a condition compares it with `!==` to the variable that holds the last layout, and an assignment stores it in that variable; the list is read by its length, and a delivery of the first revision reads it as empty. A name the enum does not declare, and a list past its bound of four, do not fit the schema: the delivery is refused whole, nothing is written, and error.execution says so, counted by `refusals`. Expected values are derived from the document, not observed from a backend.

steps.note: each variable starts at the value its expr names
a week, from a delivery of the first revision: the guard on the agenda is false, the layout changes, and the list the second revision added reads empty
an agenda with two marks: the guard compares the enum field with the variant and takes the first transition
a day with one mark: the field differs from the variable that holds the last layout, which takes it
the same day again, from a delivery of the first revision: the field equals the variable, so nothing changes but the count of marks and of screens
an agenda from a delivery of the first revision takes the guarded transition as one of the second does
a name the enum does not declare is no value of it: the delivery is refused whole, nothing is written, and error.execution says so
five marks, past the list's bound of four: refused the same way, though the enum field is a variant
a well formed payload after the refused ones is read as any other
